scenarios.title: Hand off the wide carrier and recover inside
scenarios.objective: Coordinate recovering help rather than duplicate wide pressure.
scenarios.briefing: Gold 1 carries wide toward the Navy net. D1 is set to contain that route. YOU recover near Gold 2, the inside support attacker; C trails farther back. In this drill D1 calls that the carrier is covered. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing supplies D1’s carrier call; it is not inferred solely from proximity.

questions.prompt: Which two checks help your next recovery action?

options.text: Only how close YOU can get to Gold 1

questions.explanation: The call supports coordination, but coverage can still change.

questions.prompt: Arrange one response to D1’s call.

options.text: Hear and verify the carrier coverage
Recover in relation to that threat

questions.explanation: Communication complements seeing the play; a call does not freeze responsibilities forever.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a net-side recovery relationship with Gold 2.
questions.explanation: The reference supports inside coverage while D1 handles the wide route. Reachability requires real speed information.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 beats D1 inside. What must you reconsider?

options.text: The immediate carrier threat and Gold 2’s remaining option
The old call as though nothing changed

questions.explanation: A beaten defender can change the most urgent threat. Communicate the adjustment rather than follow the first assignment blindly.

questions.prompt: What would you communicate if your recovery changes from Gold 2 toward the puck?
questions.explanation: Describe the new threat and the responsibility someone else may need to cover.

questions.prompt: What should YOU say while D1 contains Gold 1?

options.text: I have Gold 2; tell me if Gold 1 cuts inside

questions.explanation: Name Gold 2 as the inside attacker you are helping with and ask for a call if Gold 1 cuts inside. D1’s stated call concerns Gold 1, not Gold 2.

questions.prompt: Which two events require a new recovery read?
questions.explanation: Attacker routes change which relationship is most dangerous; position alone does not finish the read.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a net-side relationship with Gold 2.
questions.explanation: This example is nearer the navy net than Gold 2 and stays separate from the wide carrier route. It illustrates the goal-side relationship; reachability and a possible handoff still depend on the moving play.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 beats D1 inside. Explain how you communicate the switch.
questions.explanation: Call the inside threat by name, release the old assignment if a teammate takes it, and recover to the more dangerous reachable lane.

scenarios.title: Hinge around a two-player forecheck
scenarios.objective: Assess a reset when the first forward lanes are covered.
scenarios.briefing: YOU control a neutral-zone regroup. Gold 1 closes your board side and Gold 2 screens the direct route to F1. D2 is deeper on the opposite side; the drill permits a D-to-D reset when available. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is deeper and across the rink from YOU?
questions.explanation: D2 is closer to Navy’s net and on the opposite side of the rink.

questions.prompt: Which two checks matter for the reset?

options.text: Whether D2 is prepared to receive
Whether Gold 1 can pressure its route
Whether a D-to-D pass is mandatory under every forecheck

questions.explanation: The reset is a permitted option, not a guaranteed solution.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possible reset assessment.

options.text: Check D2 and the lateral connection
Reset or choose another available play

questions.explanation: After a reset, the new carrier must make a new read rather than replay the old one.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different angle for the D-to-D option.
questions.explanation: A deeper angle can change Gold 1’s path to the puck. It may also cost time, so the pressure must be judged.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 leaves F1’s route to close on D2. What deserves attention?

options.text: The reset regardless of Gold 2’s movement
An assumption that both routes are still equally covered

questions.explanation: Forecheckers changing jobs can alter the first option; reassess instead of committing mechanically.

questions.prompt: What makes a reset useful rather than merely moving the same problem to D2?
questions.explanation: D2 needs time, a controllable pass and a next option different from the pressure YOU face.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate during the regroup?

options.text: D2 is deeper; I will look for the connection that keeps pressure visible

questions.explanation: The message names D2 and makes the connection conditional on the changing forecheck.

questions.prompt: Which two changes can make the D-to-D option poor?

options.text: F1 becomes a safer reachable outlet
The neutral zone remains the same size

questions.explanation: Pressure and an alternative outlet decide whether the reset helps.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a new angle between D2 and F1.
questions.explanation: This point changes the carrier connection and keeps the deeper defender in view.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 leaves F1 to close D2, but Gold 3 fills the lane. What should YOU re-read?
questions.explanation: Name Gold 3 as the new pressure and check F1, D2 and the protected side before choosing a pass.

scenarios.title: Communicate when the puck goes behind the net
scenarios.objective: Handle a stated coverage exchange without losing a slot threat.
scenarios.briefing: Gold 1 controls the puck behind the Navy net. YOU and D2 are on opposite sides. The drill’s plan has the nearest defender follow the puck side while C protects Gold 2 in the slot; no automatic side swap is assumed. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: Gold 1 is behind Navy’s goal line, beyond the goalie.
